items.q: How big is the codebase Monzo's agent works on?
items.a: Over **3,000 back-end services**, about **13,000 data-warehouse models** and dozens of ML predictors.

items.q: How did Agent Chip go viral inside Monzo?
items.a: You could **react to any Slack message with an emoji** and the agent took it as a prompt.

items.q: How much work does Agent Chip do now?
items.a: It authors **over 10% of merged PRs** and runs **1,800+ tasks a day**.

items.q: What did Monzo say LLMs really stands for?
items.a: **Lots of little multipliers**: the platform pieces that made the agent fast to build.

items.q: Which platform pieces acted as multipliers?
items.a: **Monitoring and alerting**, integrations, an easy **staging environment**, queues, database abstractions and **easy deploys**.

items.q: Why does the agent keep paying off after launch?
items.a: It becomes **a new building block**, so new use cases plug into it **cheaply**.

items.q: What did Monzo build before the remote agent?
items.a: An **MCP gateway** giving local coding agents chosen tools and knowledge with **central auth**.
In an **isolated namespace separate from production**, one **sandbox pod** per task.

items.q: What controls what the agent can reach?
items.a: The **agent image** fixes tools and credentials, and a **proxy allows only chosen egress**.

items.q: How does Monzo avoid lock-in to one model provider?
items.a: The agent box is **model-agnostic**, so they can **swap models** per purpose.

items.q: What does Agent Chip do in an incident?
items.a: Reads **logs, traces and code** and gives a **high-signal** investigation, with humans controlling how much it says.

items.q: What is the proactive on-call version?
items.a: It checks **back-end changes for data impact** before the **next batch run**.

items.q: How do non-specialists use the agent?
items.a: They get a **staging-tested draft**, then involve an **engineer for review and deploy**.
